**Taco John's International, Inc.** is an American [fast food restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_food_restaurant "Fast food restaurant"). The chain serves [Mexican-inspired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuisine_of_Mexico##Mexican_food_outside_Mexico "Cuisine of Mexico")[fast food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast-food "Fast-food") as well as the company's [signature dish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature_dish "Signature dish"), Potato Olés, which are bite-sized deep-fried potato nuggets coated with a proprietary blend of seasonings.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-The_State-2) Since 2025, the company has been headquartered in [St. Louis Park, Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Park,_Minnesota "St. Louis Park, Minnesota").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-3)

As of 2022, the restaurant chain had 380 restaurants in about 22 states,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-all-locations-1) primarily in the [Midwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") and [Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_States "Mountain States") regions.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early days

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early days")]

Taco John's started in 1968 as a trailer called Taco House, run by John Turner.

Turner was an officer in the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") who served during the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War") and was an aspiring [entrepreneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneurship "Entrepreneurship"); he was stationed at [FE Warren AFB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_E._Warren_Air_Force_Base "Francis E. Warren Air Force Base"). Initially, Turner wanted to find a physical location for a [taco stand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_stand "Taco stand"). He went to James Woodson to find a location to lease, and Woodson redirected him to Harold W. Holmes, who converted one of his campers into a 12x30 trailer in seven days.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:1-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-kingfm.com-6) This was popular at [Cheyenne Frontier Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne_Frontier_Days "Cheyenne Frontier Days").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-kingfm.com-6) By the end of the year, the first official taco stand opened on the corner of Carey Ave and W 24th St (not to be confused with the first brick-and-mortar location a block away), continuing under the Taco House brand.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-tacojohnsfranchise.com-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-Derdak_2004-8)

### Name change, franchising, and growth

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Name change, franchising, and growth")]

Turner began the shift to a [franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franchising "Franchising") in 1969 by selling the franchise rights to Woodson and Holmes, who changed the name to Taco John's in honor of Turner and opened a franchise store under the Taco John's banner.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-9) They also launched Woodson-Holmes Enterprises, which gave Woodson the restaurant franchise rights, and the company name became Taco John's International, Inc. The new franchise location featured Taco John's original [mascot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mascot "Mascot"), a devil, and displayed the tagline "the hottest spot in town".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-tacojohnsfranchise.com-7)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-10) More locations opened in 1969, including the [Loveland, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loveland,_Colorado "Loveland, Colorado"), location on Lincoln Avenue.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-11)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Taco_Johns_Athens_OH_USA.JPG/250px-Taco_Johns_Athens_OH_USA.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taco_Johns_Athens_OH_USA.JPG)

Taco John's freestanding unit in [Athens, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens,_Ohio "Athens, Ohio"), with [Pizza Hut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizza_Hut "Pizza Hut")

This led to more growth of the brand in the 1970s, with many new locations opening, including the 100th store in [Scottsbluff, Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsbluff,_Nebraska "Scottsbluff, Nebraska"), in 1975.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:3-12) In 1973, the first physical brick-and-mortar, in-the-ground Taco John's was built at Carey Ave and W 23rd St in Cheyenne, Wyoming, including a [drive-through](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drive-through "Drive-through"). The original Taco John's building was moved to S Greeley Hwy and I-80, where it was demolished, but there is still a Taco John's at that location today.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:1-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:3-12)

Due to large growth, Taco John's upgraded its Cheyenne headquarters in 1985. The [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa "Iowa")-based franchise was the first to gain over $1 million in sales in 1994.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:3-12)

### Brand partnerships with some challenges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Brand partnerships with some challenges")]

[![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/63/Goodtimes-TacoJohns.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Goodtimes-TacoJohns.JPG)

Good Times/Taco John's combination restaurant in [Commerce City, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commerce_City,_Colorado "Commerce City, Colorado"), replaced and now demolished for a Starbucks.

By 2004, Taco John's began a new form of expansion normally seen in larger brands, involving partnerships with other restaurants, including local brands like [Good Times Burgers & Frozen Custard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Times_Burgers_&_Frozen_Custard "Good Times Burgers & Frozen Custard") and [Steak Escape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steak_Escape "Steak Escape") in 2004[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-14) and an [Arby's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arby's "Arby's") in [Lindenhurst, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindenhurst,_New_York "Lindenhurst, New York"), that opened in 2015.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-15)

While some of these combo stores still exist, including the Taco John's/Steak Escape Combo at Logan St and E 58th Ave in [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-16) many have either embarked on a solo journey as the Cheyenne Taco John's did after Good Times disappeared around 2010,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-18) or even completely shuttered, as in [Commerce City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commerce_City,_Colorado "Commerce City, Colorado").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-20)

Around the same time that some of these combo restaurants were closing, the original franchise owners were reaching their final days. Woodson died at age 87 in 2008 in [Scottsdale, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsdale,_Arizona "Scottsdale, Arizona").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-21) Holmes died in 2012 of heart complications at age 92 in a hospital in [Phoenix, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix,_Arizona "Phoenix, Arizona").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-22)

### Subsequent booms and challenges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Subsequent booms and challenges")]

Although Taco John's targeted smaller [Midwestern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") and [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_United_States "Western United States") communities in its early years, the chain also began expanding its presence in larger metropolitan areas like Denver and [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_metropolitan_area "Kansas City metropolitan area"), where it had a minor presence since the 1980s.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-23) Taco John's also operates several outlets serving the U.S. Armed Forces through the [Army and Air Force Exchange Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_and_Air_Force_Exchange_Service "Army and Air Force Exchange Service") (AAFES).

While some Taco John's have closed, others have opened, and new experiments have arisen. For example, in 2016, Taco John's saw its first [Love's Travel Stop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love's "Love's") location open in [Liberal, Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal,_Kansas "Liberal, Kansas").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-24) This was not the first instance of a Travel Stop combo, with one of the more recent Taco John's opening in the Loves Travel Center of [Berthoud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berthoud,_Colorado "Berthoud, Colorado") in 2018.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-25)

In April 2016, the company announced a deal to open 40 new stores in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)") and [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"). The deal includes 20 stores in the [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") area and the Northeast with an option for 15 more.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-26) As of October 2016, the company had 390 restaurants spread throughout Wyoming and 24 other states.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-27) As of August 2021, there is only one New York location, in [JFK airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_International_Airport "John F. Kennedy International Airport").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-28)[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_]

In 2017, Taco John's opened 10 new locations and expanded to Tennessee and Indiana. In 2019, it planned to open new locations in central [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)"), [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina") and [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-29)

As of August 2021, there are 380 locations,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-all-locations-1) with more planned.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-30)

In 2022, Taco John's filed suit against a small Minnesota restaurant chain, Taco Chon, which it accused of stealing its image and likeness.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-tacochon-31)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Building prototypes")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Taco_Johns_Bristol%2C_VA_%2829709562167%29.jpg/250px-Taco_Johns_Bristol%2C_VA_%2829709562167%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taco_Johns_Bristol,_VA_(29709562167).jpg)

Taco John's has had many different styles over the years. Their most recent one is best reflected by the Cheyenne restaurant,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-32) the first location to use this specific style, rebuilt in 2019.

## Trademarks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Trademarks")]

Taco John's has adopted and trademarked the term "West-Mex" to describe their food and service attitude.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-Arellano_2013-33) The company defines "West-Mex" food as having fresh, bold flavors, including their [signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature_dish "Signature dish") "Potato Olés", sauces, spices, and salsas.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-The_State-2)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-34)

In 1989, the company trademarked the phrase "[Taco Tuesday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Tuesday "Taco Tuesday")" in every U.S. state except New Jersey, where another restaurant had already trademarked it. As of 2023, Taco John's had abandoned its trademark on the phrase.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-35)

## Advertising, mascots, slogans, and logos

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Advertising, mascots, slogans, and logos")]

### Mascots

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Mascots")]

Taco John's early [mascot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mascot "Mascot"), depicted on their street signage above the words "The Hottest Spot In Town," was a devil character. Later mascots were versions of a cartoonish Mexican character named Juan with a giant [sombrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sombrero "Sombrero") and a [donkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donkey "Donkey") named Pépé.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-36) That figure was replaced in the mid-1990s by a more modern, artistic image.

Taco John's recent advertising icons have included [Whiplash the Cowboy Monkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whiplash_the_Cowboy_Monkey "Whiplash the Cowboy Monkey"), a popular rodeo attraction and PRCA Entertainer of the Year, who rides on his dog Ben to the rescue of hungry taco lovers.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-37)

Punk band In Defence performed their song "Call More Dudes" in a Taco John's as part of a tribute to the franchise.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-38)

In the 1990s, Taco John's slogan was "A Whole Lotta Mexican," which accompanied a jingle that stated "Once we getcha, then we gotcha.... gotcha coming back for more! Taco John's."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-39)

## Criticisms and controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Criticisms and controversies")]

### 2006 _E. coli_ outbreak

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2006 E. coli outbreak")]

In December 2006, a reported 50 people became sick and 18 people were hospitalized after eating at a Taco John's restaurant in Iowa. Shortly after that, [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota "Minnesota") health officials reported that an additional 27 people became ill after eating at Taco John's restaurants in [Rio Grande City, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Grande_City,_Texas "Rio Grande City, Texas"), and [Grand Forks, North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Forks,_North_Dakota "Grand Forks, North Dakota").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-40) On December 14, [Black Hawk County, Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Hawk_County,_Iowa "Black Hawk County, Iowa") health officials stated that [lettuce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lettuce "Lettuce") tainted with _[E. coli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escherichia\_coli "Escherichia coli")_ had been discovered in the supply chain. That same day, a Cedar Falls couple filed a lawsuit against Taco John's after their 9-year-old daughter was hospitalized for symptoms of _E. coli_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-41) Taco John's dropped its produce supplier, Bix Produce of [Grand Forks, North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Forks,_North_Dakota "Grand Forks, North Dakota"), as a result of the outbreaks. After a thorough investigation by the Minnesota Department of Health and the FDA, Bix Produce was cleared of any wrongdoing in the matter. The source of the outbreak was traced back to the growing fields in California. This incident came about at the same time as an unrelated _E. coli_ outbreak at [Taco Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Bell "Taco Bell") restaurants in the midwestern United States.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-42)

### 2014 nametag incident

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2014 nametag incident")]

In June 2014, Tyler Brandt, a 16-year-old employee at a Taco John's in [Yankton, South Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankton,_South_Dakota "Yankton, South Dakota"), quit his job due to his supervisor's alleged use of [homophobic slurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homophobia "Homophobia"). Brandt said his supervisor pressured him to wear a nametag that identified him as "Gaytard", and used that term to address him in front of customers and other employees. According to the Yankton store's general manager, Brandt chose the nickname for himself, and wasn't forced to wear the nametag.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-Yankton_Daily-43)

In September 2014, the [ACLU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACLU "ACLU") assisted Brandt in filing a federal discrimination charge with the [Equal Employment Opportunity Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Equal_Employment_Opportunity_Commission "United States Equal Employment Opportunity Commission"),[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-ACLU_News-44) alleging that Taco John's violated the South Dakota Human Rights Act.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-ACLU_Ohio-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-46) Taco John's addressed the incident on its Facebook page, writing that it shares the belief that discrimination is wrong, but clarifying that the franchisor does not control its franchisees' day-to-day operations or personnel decisions.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-47)

### 2023 Taco Bell lawsuit over "Taco Tuesday" trademark

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2023 Taco Bell lawsuit over \"Taco Tuesday\" trademark")]

Main article: [Taco Tuesday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Tuesday "Taco Tuesday")

Taco John's obtained a [trademark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trademark "Trademark") for the phrase "Taco Tuesday" in 1989.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:0-48) On May 16, 2023, [Taco Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Bell "Taco Bell") filed a petition with the [United States Patent and Trademark Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Patent_and_Trademark_Office "United States Patent and Trademark Office") to cancel the trademark, claiming "Taco Tuesday" was a commonplace saying and legally unavailable for trademark.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:2-50)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:0-48) Taco Bell did not seek any damages from Taco John's.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:2-50)

Taco John's CEO Jim Creel responded, "I'd like to thank our worthy competitors at Taco Bell for reminding everyone that Taco Tuesday is best celebrated at Taco John's."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:2-50)

In July 2023, Taco John's abandoned its trademark for the phrase, making it available for anyone to use. Creel said, "Paying millions of dollars to lawyers to defend our mark just doesn't feel like the right thing to do."[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-52)

**Taco John's International, Inc.** is an American [fast food restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_food_restaurant "Fast food restaurant"). The chain serves [Mexican-inspired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuisine_of_Mexico##Mexican_food_outside_Mexico "Cuisine of Mexico")[fast food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast-food "Fast-food") as well as the company's [signature dish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature_dish "Signature dish"), Potato Olés, which are bite-sized deep-fried potato nuggets coated with a proprietary blend of seasonings.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-The_State-2) Since 2025, the company has been headquartered in [St. Louis Park, Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Park,_Minnesota "St. Louis Park, Minnesota").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-3)

As of 2022, the restaurant chain had 380 restaurants in about 22 states,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-all-locations-1) primarily in the [Midwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") and [Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_States "Mountain States") regions.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early days

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early days")]

Taco John's started in 1968 as a trailer called Taco House, run by John Turner.

Turner was an officer in the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") who served during the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War") and was an aspiring [entrepreneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneurship "Entrepreneurship"); he was stationed at [FE Warren AFB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_E._Warren_Air_Force_Base "Francis E. Warren Air Force Base"). Initially, Turner wanted to find a physical location for a [taco stand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_stand "Taco stand"). He went to James Woodson to find a location to lease, and Woodson redirected him to Harold W. Holmes, who converted one of his campers into a 12x30 trailer in seven days.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:1-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-kingfm.com-6) This was popular at [Cheyenne Frontier Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne_Frontier_Days "Cheyenne Frontier Days").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-kingfm.com-6) By the end of the year, the first official taco stand opened on the corner of Carey Ave and W 24th St (not to be confused with the first brick-and-mortar location a block away), continuing under the Taco House brand.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-tacojohnsfranchise.com-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-Derdak_2004-8)

### Name change, franchising, and growth

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Name change, franchising, and growth")]

Turner began the shift to a [franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franchising "Franchising") in 1969 by selling the franchise rights to Woodson and Holmes, who changed the name to Taco John's in honor of Turner and opened a franchise store under the Taco John's banner.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-9) They also launched Woodson-Holmes Enterprises, which gave Woodson the restaurant franchise rights, and the company name became Taco John's International, Inc. The new franchise location featured Taco John's original [mascot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mascot "Mascot"), a devil, and displayed the tagline "the hottest spot in town".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-tacojohnsfranchise.com-7)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-10) More locations opened in 1969, including the [Loveland, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loveland,_Colorado "Loveland, Colorado"), location on Lincoln Avenue.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-11)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Taco_Johns_Athens_OH_USA.JPG/250px-Taco_Johns_Athens_OH_USA.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taco_Johns_Athens_OH_USA.JPG)

Taco John's freestanding unit in [Athens, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens,_Ohio "Athens, Ohio"), with [Pizza Hut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizza_Hut "Pizza Hut")

This led to more growth of the brand in the 1970s, with many new locations opening, including the 100th store in [Scottsbluff, Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsbluff,_Nebraska "Scottsbluff, Nebraska"), in 1975.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:3-12) In 1973, the first physical brick-and-mortar, in-the-ground Taco John's was built at Carey Ave and W 23rd St in Cheyenne, Wyoming, including a [drive-through](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drive-through "Drive-through"). The original Taco John's building was moved to S Greeley Hwy and I-80, where it was demolished, but there is still a Taco John's at that location today.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:1-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:3-12)

Due to large growth, Taco John's upgraded its Cheyenne headquarters in 1985. The [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa "Iowa")-based franchise was the first to gain over $1 million in sales in 1994.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:3-12)

### Brand partnerships with some challenges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Brand partnerships with some challenges")]

[![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/63/Goodtimes-TacoJohns.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Goodtimes-TacoJohns.JPG)

Good Times/Taco John's combination restaurant in [Commerce City, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commerce_City,_Colorado "Commerce City, Colorado"), replaced and now demolished for a Starbucks.

By 2004, Taco John's began a new form of expansion normally seen in larger brands, involving partnerships with other restaurants, including local brands like [Good Times Burgers & Frozen Custard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Times_Burgers_&_Frozen_Custard "Good Times Burgers & Frozen Custard") and [Steak Escape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steak_Escape "Steak Escape") in 2004[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-14) and an [Arby's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arby's "Arby's") in [Lindenhurst, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindenhurst,_New_York "Lindenhurst, New York"), that opened in 2015.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-15)

While some of these combo stores still exist, including the Taco John's/Steak Escape Combo at Logan St and E 58th Ave in [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-16) many have either embarked on a solo journey as the Cheyenne Taco John's did after Good Times disappeared around 2010,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-18) or even completely shuttered, as in [Commerce City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commerce_City,_Colorado "Commerce City, Colorado").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-20)

Around the same time that some of these combo restaurants were closing, the original franchise owners were reaching their final days. Woodson died at age 87 in 2008 in [Scottsdale, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsdale,_Arizona "Scottsdale, Arizona").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-21) Holmes died in 2012 of heart complications at age 92 in a hospital in [Phoenix, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix,_Arizona "Phoenix, Arizona").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-22)

### Subsequent booms and challenges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Subsequent booms and challenges")]

Although Taco John's targeted smaller [Midwestern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") and [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_United_States "Western United States") communities in its early years, the chain also began expanding its presence in larger metropolitan areas like Denver and [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_metropolitan_area "Kansas City metropolitan area"), where it had a minor presence since the 1980s.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-23) Taco John's also operates several outlets serving the U.S. Armed Forces through the [Army and Air Force Exchange Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_and_Air_Force_Exchange_Service "Army and Air Force Exchange Service") (AAFES).

While some Taco John's have closed, others have opened, and new experiments have arisen. For example, in 2016, Taco John's saw its first [Love's Travel Stop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love's "Love's") location open in [Liberal, Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal,_Kansas "Liberal, Kansas").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-24) This was not the first instance of a Travel Stop combo, with one of the more recent Taco John's opening in the Loves Travel Center of [Berthoud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berthoud,_Colorado "Berthoud, Colorado") in 2018.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-25)

In April 2016, the company announced a deal to open 40 new stores in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)") and [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"). The deal includes 20 stores in the [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") area and the Northeast with an option for 15 more.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-26) As of October 2016, the company had 390 restaurants spread throughout Wyoming and 24 other states.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-27) As of August 2021, there is only one New York location, in [JFK airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_International_Airport "John F. Kennedy International Airport").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-28)[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_]

In 2017, Taco John's opened 10 new locations and expanded to Tennessee and Indiana. In 2019, it planned to open new locations in central [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)"), [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina") and [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-29)

As of August 2021, there are 380 locations,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-all-locations-1) with more planned.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-30)

In 2022, Taco John's filed suit against a small Minnesota restaurant chain, Taco Chon, which it accused of stealing its image and likeness.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-tacochon-31)

## Trademarks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Trademarks")]

Taco John's has adopted and trademarked the term "West-Mex" to describe their food and service attitude.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-Arellano_2013-33) The company defines "West-Mex" food as having fresh, bold flavors, including their [signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature_dish "Signature dish") "Potato Olés", sauces, spices, and salsas.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-The_State-2)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-34)

In 1989, the company trademarked the phrase "[Taco Tuesday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Tuesday "Taco Tuesday")" in every U.S. state except New Jersey, where another restaurant had already trademarked it. As of 2023, Taco John's had abandoned its trademark on the phrase.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-35)

## Advertising, mascots, slogans, and logos

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Advertising, mascots, slogans, and logos")]

### Mascots

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Mascots")]

Taco John's early [mascot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mascot "Mascot"), depicted on their street signage above the words "The Hottest Spot In Town," was a devil character. Later mascots were versions of a cartoonish Mexican character named Juan with a giant [sombrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sombrero "Sombrero") and a [donkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donkey "Donkey") named Pépé.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-36) That figure was replaced in the mid-1990s by a more modern, artistic image.

Taco John's recent advertising icons have included [Whiplash the Cowboy Monkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whiplash_the_Cowboy_Monkey "Whiplash the Cowboy Monkey"), a popular rodeo attraction and PRCA Entertainer of the Year, who rides on his dog Ben to the rescue of hungry taco lovers.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-37)

Punk band In Defence performed their song "Call More Dudes" in a Taco John's as part of a tribute to the franchise.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-38)

In the 1990s, Taco John's slogan was "A Whole Lotta Mexican," which accompanied a jingle that stated "Once we getcha, then we gotcha.... gotcha coming back for more! Taco John's."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-39)

## Criticisms and controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Criticisms and controversies")]

### 2006 _E. coli_ outbreak

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2006 E. coli outbreak")]

In December 2006, a reported 50 people became sick and 18 people were hospitalized after eating at a Taco John's restaurant in Iowa. Shortly after that, [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota "Minnesota") health officials reported that an additional 27 people became ill after eating at Taco John's restaurants in [Rio Grande City, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Grande_City,_Texas "Rio Grande City, Texas"), and [Grand Forks, North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Forks,_North_Dakota "Grand Forks, North Dakota").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-40) On December 14, [Black Hawk County, Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Hawk_County,_Iowa "Black Hawk County, Iowa") health officials stated that [lettuce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lettuce "Lettuce") tainted with _[E. coli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escherichia\_coli "Escherichia coli")_ had been discovered in the supply chain. That same day, a Cedar Falls couple filed a lawsuit against Taco John's after their 9-year-old daughter was hospitalized for symptoms of _E. coli_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-41) Taco John's dropped its produce supplier, Bix Produce of [Grand Forks, North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Forks,_North_Dakota "Grand Forks, North Dakota"), as a result of the outbreaks. After a thorough investigation by the Minnesota Department of Health and the FDA, Bix Produce was cleared of any wrongdoing in the matter. The source of the outbreak was traced back to the growing fields in California. This incident came about at the same time as an unrelated _E. coli_ outbreak at [Taco Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Bell "Taco Bell") restaurants in the midwestern United States.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-42)

### 2014 nametag incident

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2014 nametag incident")]

In June 2014, Tyler Brandt, a 16-year-old employee at a Taco John's in [Yankton, South Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankton,_South_Dakota "Yankton, South Dakota"), quit his job due to his supervisor's alleged use of [homophobic slurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homophobia "Homophobia"). Brandt said his supervisor pressured him to wear a nametag that identified him as "Gaytard", and used that term to address him in front of customers and other employees. According to the Yankton store's general manager, Brandt chose the nickname for himself, and wasn't forced to wear the nametag.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-Yankton_Daily-43)

In September 2014, the [ACLU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACLU "ACLU") assisted Brandt in filing a federal discrimination charge with the [Equal Employment Opportunity Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Equal_Employment_Opportunity_Commission "United States Equal Employment Opportunity Commission"),[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-ACLU_News-44) alleging that Taco John's violated the South Dakota Human Rights Act.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-ACLU_Ohio-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-46) Taco John's addressed the incident on its Facebook page, writing that it shares the belief that discrimination is wrong, but clarifying that the franchisor does not control its franchisees' day-to-day operations or personnel decisions.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-47)

### 2023 Taco Bell lawsuit over "Taco Tuesday" trademark

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2023 Taco Bell lawsuit over \"Taco Tuesday\" trademark")]

Main article: [Taco Tuesday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Tuesday "Taco Tuesday")

Taco John's obtained a [trademark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trademark "Trademark") for the phrase "Taco Tuesday" in 1989.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:0-48) On May 16, 2023, [Taco Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Bell "Taco Bell") filed a petition with the [United States Patent and Trademark Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Patent_and_Trademark_Office "United States Patent and Trademark Office") to cancel the trademark, claiming "Taco Tuesday" was a commonplace saying and legally unavailable for trademark.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:2-50)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:0-48) Taco Bell did not seek any damages from Taco John's.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:2-50)

Taco John's CEO Jim Creel responded, "I'd like to thank our worthy competitors at Taco Bell for reminding everyone that Taco Tuesday is best celebrated at Taco John's."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-:2-50)

In July 2023, Taco John's abandoned its trademark for the phrase, making it available for anyone to use. Creel said, "Paying millions of dollars to lawyers to defend our mark just doesn't feel like the right thing to do."[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_Johns#cite_note-52)

**Gino's East** is a [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago")-based [restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restaurant "Restaurant") chain specializing in [deep-dish pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep-dish_pizza "Deep-dish pizza"). Two cab drivers opened the original location in 1966.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Gino's East was opened in 1966[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-1) by Sam Levine, Fred Bartoli, and George Loverde. Previously, they had opened the original Gino's in 1960 at 930 N. Rush Street.

They bought a building on East Superior Street "but didn't know what to put in it," Levine told a _[Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")_ reporter in 1983, when the restaurant was sold to new owners. "Then someone said, 'Put pizza in it.' But we didn't know pizza from nothing."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-2)

Gino's East served deep dish pizza at 162 E. Superior St., a block from the [Magnificent Mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnificent_Mile "Magnificent Mile"), from 1966 until 2000. In 2000, the building was torn down due to structural issues. The restaurant moved to the 600 block of North Wells just two days later.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-auto-3)

In 2003, [Buona Beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buona "Buona") built a new building at 162 E Superior St. After a few years, Buona reached out to the president of Gino's East, Jeff Himmel, in hopes of selling them the new property. Gino's returned to their original location, in a new building, in June 2006.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-auto-3)

### Alice Mae Redmond

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Alice Mae Redmond")]

Although the original owners were Italian (Loverde was born in Sicily and Bartoli was a first generation Italian American), they did not create the recipe for Gino's deep dish. Alice Mae Redmond, a Black woman originally working as a cook at Pizzeria Uno, was hired by the friends.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-4) Alice Mae had worked at competing [Pizzeria Uno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uno_Pizzeria_&_Grill "Uno Pizzeria & Grill") for 17 years, where she developed a special dough recipe. She claimed that she did not like the crust at Uno's, saying it was "too hard to push".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-auto1-5)

Alice Mae continued to work at the original Gino's and Gino's East as a pizza cook and recipe developer for 29 years, retiring in 1989.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-auto1-5) Her nephew, Glenn Hudley, continued to work as a manager.

### Writing on the walls

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Writing on the walls")]

Gino's East is famous for allowing their customers to write on their walls. The tradition started by accident in the 1970s when customers would use forks and knives to carve their initials into the tables. In an effort to save their dinnerware, employees began to encourage customers to write on the walls and even provided them with pens and markers. Now, [graffiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graffiti "Graffiti") covers every inch of the restaurant.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-auto-3) Newer locations and franchises do not allow their customers to write on their walls, making the flagship at 162 E Superior St. the only location that still upholds the tradition.

### 2015 5 Rabbit beer batch purchase

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2015 5 Rabbit beer batch purchase")]

In 2015, [5 Rabbit Brewery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_Rabbit_Brewery "5 Rabbit Brewery") announced that it would cease doing business with [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") because of his statements about Mexican immigrants.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-6) The brewery had brewed a batch of beer especially for a bar in [Trump Tower Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_Tower_Chicago "Trump Tower Chicago"), but ceased shipping the beer to the bar and stated that the beer would be renamed to '[Chinga Tu Pelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_Rabbit_Cervecer%C3%ADa#Chinga_Tu_Pelo_beer "5 Rabbit Cervecería")' (Fuck Your Hair),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-fuck-your-hair-7) in an apparent reference to [Trump's hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump's_hair "Trump's hair").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-Rotunno-9) A few days after that, Gino's East purchased that batch of beer from the brewery.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-10)

## Gino's Brewing Co.

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Gino's Brewing Co.")]

Founded in 2015, Gino's Brewing Co. opened inside of the Gino's East River North location in 2015. McMahon focused on creating beers that followed traditional brewing methods, and leans towards lower alcohol by volume beers.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-14)

In 2015, all four of the brewery's flagships won medals at the U.S. Open Beer Championship, winning over 4000 submissions. Lasalle St. Lager won a gold, Broken English won silver, Killarney Connection won bronze and Gino's Pale Ale won bronze.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-15)

## Expansion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Expansion")]

The company subsequently opened other locations in the [Chicago Metropolitan Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Metropolitan_Area "Chicago Metropolitan Area"), including [Wheaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheaton,_Illinois "Wheaton, Illinois"), [Naperville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naperville,_Illinois "Naperville, Illinois"), [Orland Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orland_Park,_Illinois "Orland Park, Illinois"), [Rolling Meadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Meadows,_Illinois "Rolling Meadows, Illinois"), [Lake Zurich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Zurich,_Illinois "Lake Zurich, Illinois"), [Deerfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deerfield,_Illinois "Deerfield, Illinois"), [Oak Lawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Lawn,_Illinois "Oak Lawn, Illinois"), and [Highland, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highland,_Lake_County,_Indiana "Highland, Lake County, Indiana"). Another location opened in downtown [Lake Geneva, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Geneva,_Wisconsin "Lake Geneva, Wisconsin"), a popular tourist destination near Illinois. The Oak Lawn location closed in 2008. The Naperville location closed in late 2010, the Deerfield location closed in 2012 and the Rolling Meadows location in 2013. There was one Gino's East location that operated in [Manhattan Beach, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Beach,_California "Manhattan Beach, California"), but closed in 1991.

Additionally, Gino's East operates a [mail-order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mail-order "Mail-order") business, where patrons can order frozen [pizzas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizzas "Pizzas") and have them shipped overnight. The company opened its first restaurant located outside the Chicago area in [Granger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granger,_Indiana "Granger, Indiana"), [Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana "Indiana"), but closed it in 2012.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-16)

The restaurant eventually moved from its Superior Street location into another space at 633 North Wells Street (in the former Chicago location of [Planet Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planet_Hollywood "Planet Hollywood")). The tradition of writing on the walls, however, remains the same in the new location. The original location on Superior Street reopened in 2007. In 2014, the River North location moved just south of 633 N. Wells to 500 N. LaSalle Street, a building previously occupied by nightclub Lasalle Power Co.

In 2014 the company announced expansion into Texas (ATX Brands acquired franchising rights to operate the chain outside the State of Illinois), with the first location outside of Chicago to be located in [The Woodlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Woodlands,_Texas "The Woodlands, Texas") with a November 2014 opening, followed by a January 2015 opening in [Willowbrook, Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willowbrook,_Houston "Willowbrook, Houston"). A San Antonio location opened sometime within the first quarter of 2015 along with an [Arlington, TX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington,_TX "Arlington, TX") location. A [Downtown Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Austin "Downtown Austin") location opened in late June 2015. The locations in Texas ([Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), [San Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio "San Antonio"), [DFW Metroplex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas%E2%80%93Fort_Worth_metroplex "Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex")) are former [Bikinis Sports Bar and Grill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bikinis_Sports_Bar_&_Grill "Bikinis Sports Bar & Grill") locations which were company-owned by ATX Brands.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-17)

### Nashville

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Nashville")]

In 2019 Gino's East opened its first Tennessee location in [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee"). Located at 311 3rd Avenue S. The new location opened in the SoBro neighborhood of Nashville, on March 14, National Pi Day. The Nashville location boasted a large outdoor patio with jumbo yard games (Jenga, horseshoes and cornhole) a late night pizza window and a dual inside and outside bar. Murals by Nashville artist Brett Hunter can also be found throughout the restaurant.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-18)

### Los Angeles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Los Angeles")]

In 2020 a franchise was opened in Los Angeles, located at 12924 Riverside Dr. Sherman Oaks, CA. The new location took over a building that originally housed Rock 'n Pies.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-19)

Today Gino's East has 10 locations.

**Gino's East** is a [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago")-based [restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restaurant "Restaurant") chain specializing in [deep-dish pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep-dish_pizza "Deep-dish pizza"). Two cab drivers opened the original location in 1966.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Gino's East was opened in 1966[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-1) by Sam Levine, Fred Bartoli, and George Loverde. Previously, they had opened the original Gino's in 1960 at 930 N. Rush Street.

They bought a building on East Superior Street "but didn't know what to put in it," Levine told a _[Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")_ reporter in 1983, when the restaurant was sold to new owners. "Then someone said, 'Put pizza in it.' But we didn't know pizza from nothing."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-2)

Gino's East served deep dish pizza at 162 E. Superior St., a block from the [Magnificent Mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnificent_Mile "Magnificent Mile"), from 1966 until 2000. In 2000, the building was torn down due to structural issues. The restaurant moved to the 600 block of North Wells just two days later.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-auto-3)

In 2003, [Buona Beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buona "Buona") built a new building at 162 E Superior St. After a few years, Buona reached out to the president of Gino's East, Jeff Himmel, in hopes of selling them the new property. Gino's returned to their original location, in a new building, in June 2006.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-auto-3)

### Alice Mae Redmond

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Alice Mae Redmond")]

Although the original owners were Italian (Loverde was born in Sicily and Bartoli was a first generation Italian American), they did not create the recipe for Gino's deep dish. Alice Mae Redmond, a Black woman originally working as a cook at Pizzeria Uno, was hired by the friends.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-4) Alice Mae had worked at competing [Pizzeria Uno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uno_Pizzeria_&_Grill "Uno Pizzeria & Grill") for 17 years, where she developed a special dough recipe. She claimed that she did not like the crust at Uno's, saying it was "too hard to push".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-auto1-5)

Alice Mae continued to work at the original Gino's and Gino's East as a pizza cook and recipe developer for 29 years, retiring in 1989.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-auto1-5) Her nephew, Glenn Hudley, continued to work as a manager.

### Writing on the walls

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Writing on the walls")]

Gino's East is famous for allowing their customers to write on their walls. The tradition started by accident in the 1970s when customers would use forks and knives to carve their initials into the tables. In an effort to save their dinnerware, employees began to encourage customers to write on the walls and even provided them with pens and markers. Now, [graffiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graffiti "Graffiti") covers every inch of the restaurant.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-auto-3) Newer locations and franchises do not allow their customers to write on their walls, making the flagship at 162 E Superior St. the only location that still upholds the tradition.

### 2015 5 Rabbit beer batch purchase

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2015 5 Rabbit beer batch purchase")]

In 2015, [5 Rabbit Brewery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_Rabbit_Brewery "5 Rabbit Brewery") announced that it would cease doing business with [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") because of his statements about Mexican immigrants.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-6) The brewery had brewed a batch of beer especially for a bar in [Trump Tower Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_Tower_Chicago "Trump Tower Chicago"), but ceased shipping the beer to the bar and stated that the beer would be renamed to '[Chinga Tu Pelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_Rabbit_Cervecer%C3%ADa#Chinga_Tu_Pelo_beer "5 Rabbit Cervecería")' (Fuck Your Hair),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-fuck-your-hair-7) in an apparent reference to [Trump's hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump's_hair "Trump's hair").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-Rotunno-9) A few days after that, Gino's East purchased that batch of beer from the brewery.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-10)

## Gino's Brewing Co.

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Gino's Brewing Co.")]

Founded in 2015, Gino's Brewing Co. opened inside of the Gino's East River North location in 2015. McMahon focused on creating beers that followed traditional brewing methods, and leans towards lower alcohol by volume beers.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-14)

In 2015, all four of the brewery's flagships won medals at the U.S. Open Beer Championship, winning over 4000 submissions. Lasalle St. Lager won a gold, Broken English won silver, Killarney Connection won bronze and Gino's Pale Ale won bronze.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-15)

## Expansion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Expansion")]

The company subsequently opened other locations in the [Chicago Metropolitan Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Metropolitan_Area "Chicago Metropolitan Area"), including [Wheaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheaton,_Illinois "Wheaton, Illinois"), [Naperville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naperville,_Illinois "Naperville, Illinois"), [Orland Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orland_Park,_Illinois "Orland Park, Illinois"), [Rolling Meadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Meadows,_Illinois "Rolling Meadows, Illinois"), [Lake Zurich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Zurich,_Illinois "Lake Zurich, Illinois"), [Deerfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deerfield,_Illinois "Deerfield, Illinois"), [Oak Lawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Lawn,_Illinois "Oak Lawn, Illinois"), and [Highland, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highland,_Lake_County,_Indiana "Highland, Lake County, Indiana"). Another location opened in downtown [Lake Geneva, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Geneva,_Wisconsin "Lake Geneva, Wisconsin"), a popular tourist destination near Illinois. The Oak Lawn location closed in 2008. The Naperville location closed in late 2010, the Deerfield location closed in 2012 and the Rolling Meadows location in 2013. There was one Gino's East location that operated in [Manhattan Beach, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Beach,_California "Manhattan Beach, California"), but closed in 1991.

Additionally, Gino's East operates a [mail-order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mail-order "Mail-order") business, where patrons can order frozen [pizzas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizzas "Pizzas") and have them shipped overnight. The company opened its first restaurant located outside the Chicago area in [Granger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granger,_Indiana "Granger, Indiana"), [Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana "Indiana"), but closed it in 2012.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-16)

The restaurant eventually moved from its Superior Street location into another space at 633 North Wells Street (in the former Chicago location of [Planet Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planet_Hollywood "Planet Hollywood")). The tradition of writing on the walls, however, remains the same in the new location. The original location on Superior Street reopened in 2007. In 2014, the River North location moved just south of 633 N. Wells to 500 N. LaSalle Street, a building previously occupied by nightclub Lasalle Power Co.

In 2014 the company announced expansion into Texas (ATX Brands acquired franchising rights to operate the chain outside the State of Illinois), with the first location outside of Chicago to be located in [The Woodlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Woodlands,_Texas "The Woodlands, Texas") with a November 2014 opening, followed by a January 2015 opening in [Willowbrook, Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willowbrook,_Houston "Willowbrook, Houston"). A San Antonio location opened sometime within the first quarter of 2015 along with an [Arlington, TX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington,_TX "Arlington, TX") location. A [Downtown Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Austin "Downtown Austin") location opened in late June 2015. The locations in Texas ([Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), [San Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio "San Antonio"), [DFW Metroplex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas%E2%80%93Fort_Worth_metroplex "Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex")) are former [Bikinis Sports Bar and Grill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bikinis_Sports_Bar_&_Grill "Bikinis Sports Bar & Grill") locations which were company-owned by ATX Brands.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-17)

### Nashville

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Nashville")]

In 2019 Gino's East opened its first Tennessee location in [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee"). Located at 311 3rd Avenue S. The new location opened in the SoBro neighborhood of Nashville, on March 14, National Pi Day. The Nashville location boasted a large outdoor patio with jumbo yard games (Jenga, horseshoes and cornhole) a late night pizza window and a dual inside and outside bar. Murals by Nashville artist Brett Hunter can also be found throughout the restaurant.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-18)

### Los Angeles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino%27s_East&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Los Angeles")]

In 2020 a franchise was opened in Los Angeles, located at 12924 Riverside Dr. Sherman Oaks, CA. The new location took over a building that originally housed Rock 'n Pies.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino's_East#cite_note-19)

Today Gino's East has 10 locations.

**Taco John's International, Inc.** is an American [fast food restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_food_restaurant "Fast food restaurant"). The chain serves [Mexican-inspired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuisine_of_Mexico##Mexican_food_outside_Mexico "Cuisine of Mexico")[fast food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast-food "Fast-food") as well as the company's [signature dish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature_dish "Signature dish"), Potato Olés, which are bite-sized deep-fried potato nuggets coated with a proprietary blend of seasonings.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-The_State-2) Since 2025, the company has been headquartered in [St. Louis Park, Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Park,_Minnesota "St. Louis Park, Minnesota").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-3)

As of 2022, the restaurant chain had 380 restaurants in about 22 states,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-all-locations-1) primarily in the [Midwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") and [Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_States "Mountain States") regions.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early days

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early days")]

Taco John's started in 1968 as a trailer called Taco House, run by John Turner.

Turner was an officer in the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") who served during the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War") and was an aspiring [entrepreneur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrepreneurship "Entrepreneurship"); he was stationed at [FE Warren AFB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_E._Warren_Air_Force_Base "Francis E. Warren Air Force Base"). Initially, Turner wanted to find a physical location for a [taco stand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_stand "Taco stand"). He went to James Woodson to find a location to lease, and Woodson redirected him to Harold W. Holmes, who converted one of his campers into a 12x30 trailer in seven days.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-:1-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-kingfm.com-6) This was popular at [Cheyenne Frontier Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne_Frontier_Days "Cheyenne Frontier Days").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-kingfm.com-6) By the end of the year, the first official taco stand opened on the corner of Carey Ave and W 24th St (not to be confused with the first brick-and-mortar location a block away), continuing under the Taco House brand.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-tacojohnsfranchise.com-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-Derdak_2004-8)

### Name change, franchising, and growth

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Name change, franchising, and growth")]

Turner began the shift to a [franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franchising "Franchising") in 1969 by selling the franchise rights to Woodson and Holmes, who changed the name to Taco John's in honor of Turner and opened a franchise store under the Taco John's banner.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-9) They also launched Woodson-Holmes Enterprises, which gave Woodson the restaurant franchise rights, and the company name became Taco John's International, Inc. The new franchise location featured Taco John's original [mascot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mascot "Mascot"), a devil, and displayed the tagline "the hottest spot in town".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-tacojohnsfranchise.com-7)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-10) More locations opened in 1969, including the [Loveland, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loveland,_Colorado "Loveland, Colorado"), location on Lincoln Avenue.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-11)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Taco_Johns_Athens_OH_USA.JPG/250px-Taco_Johns_Athens_OH_USA.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taco_Johns_Athens_OH_USA.JPG)

Taco John's freestanding unit in [Athens, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens,_Ohio "Athens, Ohio"), with [Pizza Hut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizza_Hut "Pizza Hut")

This led to more growth of the brand in the 1970s, with many new locations opening, including the 100th store in [Scottsbluff, Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsbluff,_Nebraska "Scottsbluff, Nebraska"), in 1975.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-:3-12) In 1973, the first physical brick-and-mortar, in-the-ground Taco John's was built at Carey Ave and W 23rd St in Cheyenne, Wyoming, including a [drive-through](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drive-through "Drive-through"). The original Taco John's building was moved to S Greeley Hwy and I-80, where it was demolished, but there is still a Taco John's at that location today.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-:1-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-:3-12)

Due to large growth, Taco John's upgraded its Cheyenne headquarters in 1985. The [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa "Iowa")-based franchise was the first to gain over $1 million in sales in 1994.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-:3-12)

### Brand partnerships with some challenges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Brand partnerships with some challenges")]

[![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/63/Goodtimes-TacoJohns.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Goodtimes-TacoJohns.JPG)

Good Times/Taco John's combination restaurant in [Commerce City, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commerce_City,_Colorado "Commerce City, Colorado"), replaced and now demolished for a Starbucks.

By 2004, Taco John's began a new form of expansion normally seen in larger brands, involving partnerships with other restaurants, including local brands like [Good Times Burgers & Frozen Custard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Times_Burgers_&_Frozen_Custard "Good Times Burgers & Frozen Custard") and [Steak Escape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steak_Escape "Steak Escape") in 2004[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-14) and an [Arby's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arby's "Arby's") in [Lindenhurst, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindenhurst,_New_York "Lindenhurst, New York"), that opened in 2015.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-15)

While some of these combo stores still exist, including the Taco John's/Steak Escape Combo at Logan St and E 58th Ave in [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-16) many have either embarked on a solo journey as the Cheyenne Taco John's did after Good Times disappeared around 2010,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-18) or even completely shuttered, as in [Commerce City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commerce_City,_Colorado "Commerce City, Colorado").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-20)

Around the same time that some of these combo restaurants were closing, the original franchise owners were reaching their final days. Woodson died at age 87 in 2008 in [Scottsdale, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsdale,_Arizona "Scottsdale, Arizona").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-21) Holmes died in 2012 of heart complications at age 92 in a hospital in [Phoenix, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix,_Arizona "Phoenix, Arizona").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-22)

### Subsequent booms and challenges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Taco_John%27s&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Subsequent booms and challenges")]

Although Taco John's targeted smaller [Midwestern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") and [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_United_States "Western United States") communities in its early years, the chain also began expanding its presence in larger metropolitan areas like Denver and [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_metropolitan_area "Kansas City metropolitan area"), where it had a minor presence since the 1980s.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-23) Taco John's also operates several outlets serving the U.S. Armed Forces through the [Army and Air Force Exchange Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_and_Air_Force_Exchange_Service "Army and Air Force Exchange Service") (AAFES).

While some Taco John's have closed, others have opened, and new experiments have arisen. For example, in 2016, Taco John's saw its first [Love's Travel Stop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love's "Love's") location open in [Liberal, Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal,_Kansas "Liberal, Kansas").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-24) This was not the first instance of a Travel Stop combo, with one of the more recent Taco John's opening in the Loves Travel Center of [Berthoud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berthoud,_Colorado "Berthoud, Colorado") in 2018.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-25)

In April 2016, the company announced a deal to open 40 new stores in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)") and [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"). The deal includes 20 stores in the [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") area and the Northeast with an option for 15 more.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-26) As of October 2016, the company had 390 restaurants spread throughout Wyoming and 24 other states.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-27) As of August 2021, there is only one New York location, in [JFK airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_International_Airport "John F. Kennedy International Airport").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-28)[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_]

In 2017, Taco John's opened 10 new locations and expanded to Tennessee and Indiana. In 2019, it planned to open new locations in central [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)"), [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina") and [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-29)

As of August 2021, there are 380 locations,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-all-locations-1) with more planned.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-30)

In 2022, Taco John's filed suit against a small Minnesota restaurant chain, Taco Chon, which it accused of stealing its image and likeness.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taco_John's#cite_note-tacochon-31)
